text:
alex_support: FYI ticket #4521 — customer reports invoice shows ~1.2M tokens but their dashboard shows ~900k. They think we're overbilling. Can someone triage?

maria_billing: Can you paste invoice id + sample line items? Also which org id? I'll pull billing ledger.

alex_support: Invoice INV-2026-04521, org: org-acme-9. Quick snippet from the invoice CSV: 

```
2026-02-24,org-acme-9,model:rw-large,served_tokens,1,200,345
2026-02-24,org-acme-9,model:rw-large,metered_tokens,900,123
```

Link to dashboard export: https://dash.redwood.dev/org-acme-9/usage/export (shared privately)

oscar_engineer: Odd. Two immediate hypotheses: 1) continuous batching / prefetch caused extra "served" tokens at runtime that telemetry didn't collapse for meterable counts, or 2) double-counting from streaming abort + re-request.

priya_telemetry: Quick note — we rolled out a tiny telemetry change in last deploy (see commit 9a7c) that moved some counters earlier in the pipeline so they're emitted before KV prefetch dedupe. deploy_bot: deployed commit 9a7c to prod at 2026-02-24T03:12Z.

maria_billing: If telemetry is emitting pre-prefetch served tokens and invoicing uses model-server counters, that would explain invoice > dashboard. Need reconciliation.

oscar_engineer: Can we get a few sample request_ids from the customer? If we can grep the trace logs we can compare per-request served_tokens vs final metered tokens. Example grep: 

```
rg "request_id=([a-z0-9-]+)" /var/log/serving/* | cut -d' ' -f3 | sort | uniq -c
# then inspect JSON blobs for served_tokens / metered_tokens
```

alex_support: Asked customer for 3 request_ids and a time window (they provided: 2026-02-24 02:55 - 03:25 UTC). Waiting.

priya_telemetry: While we wait, I'll run an aggregate reconciliation for that org for the day. SQL I plan to run: 

```
SELECT org_id, sum(served_tokens) as served, sum(metered_tokens) as metered
FROM telemetry.request_counters
WHERE org_id='org-acme-9' AND day='2026-02-24'
GROUP BY org_id;
```

oscar_engineer: Also check the prefetch logs: `/var/log/serving/prefetch.log` — look for `prefetch_kv=true` events. Prefetch currently logs the estimated prefix tokens we warm; those are included in served counters historically.

maria_billing: If the reconciliation shows invoice source > metered sum, we need to map which pipeline fed billing. Billing uses the model-server aggregated counter (billing_stream) vs telemetry.request_counters which is post-batching. Those can diverge.

alex_support: Customer reply with request_ids: `rq_7f3a`, `rq_7f3b`, `rq_7f3c`. They say each correlates with spikes in their realtime panel.

priya_telemetry: Found matching rows for those request_ids. Quick diff for those ids: served_tokens = 12,300 total, metered_tokens = 9,100 total. That's consistent with the 1.2M vs 900k pattern.

oscar_engineer: Looks like prefetch/prefix accounted tokens are in served_tokens but later deduped in metered path. Root cause: when continuous batching prefetch invokes KV warming across batched recipients, we increment the per-request served counter before the KV cache collapse runs. In high-concurrency bursts you get one warm counted per request instead of once per prefix.

maria_billing: Confirmed — billing ingestion reads model-server `served_tokens` stream which currently doesn't apply the prefix dedupe. We'll need to either: 1) change billing to use post-dedupe metered stream, or 2) emit an adjusted counter from serving that subtracts prefetched prefix attribution.

priya_telemetry: I can run a one-off backfill to compute corrected metered totals for Feb 24 for org-acme-9 and propose a credit if diff > 2%. SQL snippet I used: 

```
WITH per_req AS (
  SELECT request_id, served_tokens, metered_tokens, prefetched_prefix_tokens
  FROM telemetry.request_counters
  WHERE day='2026-02-24' AND org_id='org-acme-9'
)
SELECT sum(served_tokens) as served, sum(metered_tokens) as metered, sum(prefetched_prefix_tokens) as prefetched
FROM per_req;
```

oscar_engineer: Longer-term I'll add a reconciler that validates billing_stream vs telemetry.post_dedupe at a daily cadence and alerts if >1% delta. I'll open an RFC for the change to pipeline.

maria_billing: For this customer, if priya's backfill shows >5% delta we should auto-issue a provisional credit and flag for manual review. I'll prepare a credit note template.

alex_support: Action items: priya run backfill (ETA 2h), oscar RFC + reconciler (ETA EOD), maria prepare credit flow, alex update customer with interim note.

deploy_bot: FYI change 9a7c (telemetry) reverted in 9b1f on 2026-02-25 due to unrelated perf regression. That revert reintroduced previous counter ordering.

priya_telemetry: Backfill done: served=1,203,444 metered=901,010 prefetched=280,120 for Feb 24. Delta ~33.6%. I'll attach reconciliation CSV to the ticket.

maria_billing: Okay — >30% is large. Issuing provisional credit for the delta and marking invoice as under review. I'll follow up with accounting for formal adjustment.

oscar_engineer: I'll start the RFC tomorrow to make billing source use post-dedupe counters (or to emit an explicit billing_counter). Also adding extra logging around `prefetch_kv=true` events for better auditing.

alex_support: Thanks team. I'll post the reconciliation CSV and close the loop with the customer. Closing notes for record: root cause = telemetry/billing source mismatch around KV prefetch + when counters are emitted during continuous batching.

maria_billing: tagging as `actioned` and `billing-credit-applied` in the ticket. :white_check_mark:

priya_telemetry: leaving a small follow-up note: we'll add a nightly job to compute `billing_adjustment` per-org for the next 30 days so we catch any other orgs affected by the 9a7c window.

alex_support: Great. Ticket updated, customer notified about provisional credit. Will monitor for any follow-ups. :thumbsup:
